 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. There are a lot of reasons why the Tampa Bay Rays have found as much success on the field this season as they have.
 The American League East champions and No. 1 seed in the AL are in a tough battle with the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS, with the series tied 1-1 heading to Progressive Field for the next three.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement One of the major contributing factors to the team winning so much is how good their defense has been. They were second in MLB in Total Defensive Runs Saved with 87, behind only the Chicago Cubs, who recorded 115. Those two teams created a massive gap with the third-place team, the Boston Red Sox, at 67.
 It should come as no surprise, then, that the Rays are well represented on the list of 2026 Rawlings Gold Glove Award Finalists. Making the list are shortstop Taylor Walls and left fielder Chandler Simpson .
 Taylor Walls, Chandler Simpson named Gold Glove finalists
 Jul 22, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Tampa Bay Rays left fielder Chandler Simpson (14) celebrates a win over the Toronto Blue Jays with shortstop Taylor Walls (6) and second baseman Ben Williamson (15) at Rogers Centre. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect
 Walls is joined by Andres Gimenez of the Toronto Blue Jays and Bobby Witt Jr. of the Kansas City Royals at shortstop. Along with Simpson in left field, the finalists are Cody Bellinger of the New York Yankees and Wyatt Langford of the Texas Rangers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Seeing Walls as a finalist comes as little surprise. He was also named a finalist when he racked up 18 Defensive Runs Saved in 2025, which was tied for sixth in MLB despite playing in only 98 games and 750.2 innings.
 This season, he was just as good. He finished in a tie for third in MLB with 21 DRS, which led all shortstops. However, not all defensive metrics are favorable for Walls, who has recorded a -2 Fielding Run Value, which falls in the 35th percentile, per Statcast, with an Outs Above Average of -3, which is in the 22nd percentile.
 Simpson being a finalist is an incredible achievement. He struggled mightily playing the outfield as a rookie in 2025 but worked tirelessly this offseason, including work with Kevin Kiermaier during spring training.
 Those reps did wonders for him, turning him into a stellar defender in left field. Simpson was in the 67th percentile with a +3 Fielding Run Value. His +8 Outs Above Average was elite in the 94th percentile.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Per Statcast, he had an 8 Defensive Runs Saved, which was tied for the seventh-best mark amongst left fielders. Simpson doesn't have a strong arm, but he more than makes up for it with his elite speed .
 Both Tampa Bay players are facing stiff competition to win a Gold Glove Award, but both are certainly deserving with how well they have played defense this season.
